## Rule

Decoded 2026-06-04. Let `M = (input == 5)`. Find:

```python
r0 = first row with any M
c0 = first col with any M
P[i, j] = M[r0 + 3*i, c0 + 3*j]      # i,j in 0..2
output_mask = kron(P, P)              # 9x9
```

Emit color 5 where `output_mask` is true, color 0 in the remaining 9x9 cells, and all-zero padding outside the 9x9. This is the block-level function; it is not a lookup over observed patterns.

## Algorithm sketch

```python
def task195_reference(grid):
    m = (np.asarray(grid) == 5)
    r0 = np.where(m.any(axis=1))[0][0]
    c0 = np.where(m.any(axis=0))[0][0]
    P = np.zeros((3, 3), dtype=np.uint8)
    for i in range(3):
        for j in range(3):
            rr, cc = r0 + 3*i, c0 + 3*j
            if rr < m.shape[0] and cc < m.shape[1]:
                P[i, j] = m[rr, cc]
    return (np.kron(P, P) * 5).tolist()
```

ONNX v1 computes the same rule with:
`Slice(input ch5, 0:23, 0:25) -> ReduceMax/ArgMax first row+col -> dynamic Gather 3 rows/3 cols -> Cast BOOL -> broadcasted And for kron(P,P) -> Where U8 labels -> Pad sentinel 10 -> Equal(label, channel_ids) BOOL output`.

## Cost analysis

LIVE cost re-measured 2026-06-04: memory 46,750 + params 1,037 = **47,787**. Dominators are output assembly, not rule logic: two `[1,10,30,30]` F16 planes (`o5`, `o0`) cost 36,000 bytes, plus single-channel full-canvas Pad/Sub planes.

`task195_v1.onnx` cost after the 17x19 source crop: memory 2,934 + params 52 = **2,986**. Main counted intermediates are the cropped ch5 source `[1,1,17,19]` F32 (1,292 B), `label30` `[1,1,30,30]` U8 (900 B), row gather `[1,1,3,19]` F32 (228 B), and small vectors/scalars. The final `[1,10,30,30]` BOOL Equal is the graph output and is not counted.

The 17x19 crop is CROP-CONTRACT safe because the task prompt and full corpus both bound inputs to 17x19. Extra check on the full 200k corpus: `r0 max=7`, `c0 max=9`, so sampled lattice coordinates satisfy `r0+6<=13`, `c0+6<=15`.

`task195_v2.onnx` cost: memory 1,765 + params 113 = **1,878**. It removes the counted source plane entirely. Dominant tensors are now the `[1,10,9,9]` BOOL one-hot patch (810 B), the INT64 GatherND index `[1,3,3,3]` (216 B), and the two row/col `Einsum` outputs `[1,30]` F32 (120 B each). The index is built as `idx_base + [0,r0,c0]`, with `batch_dims=1` supplying the batch coordinate, which avoids the larger 4-component index grid from the first v2 draft.

`task195_v3.onnx` cost: memory 1,732 + params 75 = **1,807**. Three micro-optimisations on v2 (drop `ones30`, `shape_p4`+`P_b`, `shape_offset`+offset Reshape). The v3 proof claimed the 810 B `out9_oh` one-hot patch was "forced by the 10-channel Pad-last output structure" — **this was FALSE** (see freeoutkron below).

### CURRENT BEST: `task195_f16kron.onnx` cost **489** (memory 261 + params 228) — BEATS prior best/team-best 525 by 36

**Worker w2, beta_p29_claude_cli, 2026-06-24.** Note: the team-best 525 (Boladi) has the IDENTICAL sha256 (`d3189b02...`) as our prior `hybrid_slicekron` — it IS our graph. So 525 was both our best and the team-best; beating it required a genuine new shrink.

**The single change.** The free-output separable Einsum (`output = Einsum('gtij,gtad,tk,ir,ar,jc,dc->gkrc', Q,Q,Ksel,Hb,Lb,Hb,Lb)`) reads `Q`, `Ksel`, `Hb`, `Lb` — all initializer- or Cast-derived, **NOT** the F32 graph `input`. So it is NOT subject to the task351 carrier-dtype lock (which fires only when the F32 graph input is itself an Einsum operand). ORT runs F16 Einsum (ort_reality.md:55, verified end-to-end here). Building all four operands as **F16** shrinks the only remaining F32 head tensor: `Q` F32[1,2,3,3]=72 B → F16[1,2,3,3]=36 B (**−36 memory**). Params are element-count so Hb/Lb/Ksel staying F16 doesn't change the 228 param total. Output declared F16; the decoder's `>0.0` threshold decodes F16 identically (core.md). Gates: visible 265/265, truth 200000/200000, ab byte_equal=True 200265/200265 vs LIVE, profile=489==static over 266 arcgen real inputs (no reprice gap). Staged `staged_submits/task195_cheaperkronpdetector_cost489/`.

**Next lever / WALL.** `x5f` F32[1,1,5,5]=100 B is now the dominant single charge and is FORCED: Slice of the F32 graph input inherits F32, and the 5×5 strided window is the minimum for the ArgMax-first-hit + [0,1,2] offset read (top/left ∈ {0,1,2}, need 3 consecutive of the 5 strided positions). Casting input→U8 before slicing materializes a [1,10,30,30] U8 plane (9000 B, far worse); a free-input Einsum reading the strided lattice is F32-locked and still produces the same 25 F32 cells. Hb/Lb [3,30]=180 params are the minimal #118 factorization (width 30 forced by the [1,10,30,30] output). 489 is the WALL for this anchor+free-output family absent a structurally cheaper anchor that avoids the F32 5×5 read.

## Don't-do log

- Do not build a table over observed 3x3-block patterns. The prompt records a scout result: 253 observed pattern→output pairs score 98.5% but fail the official held-out pattern. This is the visible-fail/memorization trap.
- Do not crop/mutate the LIVE graph as `[1,10,19,19]`; that prior attempt increased cost because the graph pads internally and the 10-channel crop costs more than it saves.
- Do not re-expand output with F16 channel Mul/Add planes. Use a U8 label canvas plus final BOOL `Equal(label, ids)` so the 10-channel one-hot is the graph output.
- `GatherND` indices must be INT64 under the scorer's strict shape inference; the INT32 index draft failed with `indices typestr ... unsupported type`.
- Do NOT believe the (now-deleted) v3 claim that the 810 B `out9_oh` patch is "forced by the Pad-last structure". It is not: kron is a separable self-product, the whole one-hot output is a free-output Einsum (#109/#119), and the patch is fully dissolvable — see `task195_freeoutkron` (cost 1011). Floor proofs are formulation-relative (#68): always enumerate the free-output / contraction-final family before declaring a memory floor.
